neighbours.label: third-person researchers reporting a claim: the reporting verb or subject after 'the authors/researchers/they' (concluded, suggest, propose)
fire: In the final section, the authors argue that the drug works mainly through the liver.
The researchers concluded that longer sleep improved test scores in older students.
Based on the tree rings, they estimate that the drought lasted almost twenty years.
The study's authors attribute the drop in cases to the new hand-washing rules.
In a follow-up paper, the scientists propose a simpler model of the reaction.
Using satellite images, the team reported that the glacier had shrunk by a third.
The investigators suggest that the bacteria spread through the water supply.
After reviewing the records, the historians claimed that the letter was a forgery.
quiet: In the final section, we argue that the drug works mainly through the liver.
Our data show that longer sleep improved test scores in older students.
Based on the tree rings, the drought lasted almost twenty years.
We attribute the drop in cases to the new hand-washing rules.
In a follow-up paper, we propose a simpler model of the reaction.
In satellite images from last year, the glacier had shrunk by a third.
The bacteria may have spread through the water supply last spring.
After we reviewed the records, it seemed that the letter was a forgery.

notes: card: ' authors' x5, ' they' x3, ' concluded', ' suggest', ' propose', ' attributed'. The - pole is first-person 'we/us/our' and 'unpub. data', so the distinction looks like third-person vs first-person attribution of claims. Near misses: first-person or no attribution.
